extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, grant managers, and researchers applying for/tracking NSF science education undergraduate awards
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction/interpretation of an awards listing for NSF Science Education Support showing awardees (PI), institutions, project titles, program types, award codes, durations (months), and dollar amounts. Useful for grant tracking, database entry, or applicant benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENCE EDUCATION SUPPORT (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Header/category under which the following awards are listed (e.g., '182 SCIENCE EDUCATION SUPPORT').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page groups awards under this program heading by state and institution; every entry beneath this heading is an award associated with Science Education Support. Use this as the top-level category when organizing these awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated program label appearing throughout the listing (verbatim: 'UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPATION').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically accompanied by: (award code); duration listed in MONTHS (commonly '11 MONTHS'); and a dollar amount (e.g., '$12,720'). Examples from page: 'POPE, MICHAEL T; UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPATION (Y009767); 11 MONTHS $12,720' and many similar entries across states. Use this program label to identify awards intended to support undergraduate research participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: STUDENT-ORIGINATED STUDIES / STUDENT-ORIGINATED STUDIES (variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program label for awards supporting student-originated projects (appears as 'STUDENT-ORIGINATED STUDIES', 'STUDENT-ORIGINATED, MANAGED AND PRESENTED COURSE IN SCIENCE FOR THE FRESHMAN NON-SCIENCE MAJOR', and short variants such as 'STUDENT-ORIGINATED STUDIES (Y009207 001)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries commonly show a 12-MONTH duration and a dollar amount (examples: 'PAYNE, JOHN C, AND PETERSEN, QUENTIN R; 4 STUDENT-ORIGINATED, MANAGED AND PRESENTED COURSE IN SCIENCE FOR THE FRESHMAN NON-SCIENCE MAJOR (Y009694); 12 MONTHS $8,900' and 'MULLER, THOMAS J; ECOLOGY OF THE MIDWAY WATERSHED AREA (¥009688); 12 MONTHS $10,000'). Use this label to flag awards that are specifically student-initiated or curriculum-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: OTHER PROGRAM AWARDS (O?AWDS) / NONE; OTHER PROGRAM AWARDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries or state-level lines that indicate residual/small awards labeled like 'NONE; OTHER PROGRAM AWARDS (O2AWDS), $4,125' or 'NONE; OTHER PROGRAM AWARDS (O1AWDS),; $2,075'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as miscellaneous or small-value awards not assigned to a named PI/project on the page. They are typically single-line totals for a state and may represent administrative or residual allocations. Capture as 'other' program award entries when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: AWARD METADATA FIELDS (implicit schema)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each award record on the page follows an implicit structured pattern: PI/Project Director name; project title or program label; (award code); duration in MONTHS; dollar amount; institution and state grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extracting or evaluating these records, parse and store the following fields: state, institution, PI name, project title/program label (e.g., 'UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPATION'), award code (e.g., 'Y009767' or 'AG00354'), duration (e.g., '11 MONTHS' or '12 MONTHS'), award amount (dollar value). Examples abound throughout the page (e.g., 'DAVIDSON, EDWARD S; UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPA- TION (¥009729); 11 MONTHS $15,620'). This implicit schema is the primary 'criterion' useful for downstream grant-funding tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: GEOGRAPHIC / INSTITUTIONAL GROUPING (by state and institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are organized first by U.S. state (e.g., 'FLORIDA', 'GEORGIA', 'HAWAII'), then by institution within each state (e.g., 'FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY', 'UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the state and institution headings to group or filter awards; many entries list multiple awards for a single institution. This organization implies that reporting and analysis should support grouping by state and institution.
